narrative_purpose: Shows why planetary systems are flat, and shows in the same frame the companion star cutting the disk short - the specific constraint Alpha Centauri A's disk was built under.
subject: A newborn star at the centre with a broad, thin, glowing disk of gas and dust extending outward around it, seen at a shallow angle so the disk reads as a flattened ellipse. Above and below the star, two faint funnels of infalling material descend toward it from the remains of a dark contracting cloud. On the right, at a distance, a second smaller orange star sits in open space, and the disk's outer edge on that side stops abruptly in a clean curved cut-off instead of fading gradually.
scene: The last of the parent cloud hangs as dark ragged veils around the upper and lower edges of the frame. Faint distant stars show through the gaps.
camera: Wide view from about fifteen degrees above the disk plane, star slightly left of centre, disk extending across the frame toward the companion.
light: The newborn star is the key light, brightest at the disk's inner edge and dimming outward; the companion star adds a small scarce warm glint from the right; the surrounding cloud stays deep indigo.
palette: Void-indigo space and cloud, cool cyan and teal disk brightening to mist-white near the star, one small scarce amber companion, faint warm core.
style: Painterly astronomical plate, soft and atmospheric, layered haze, no hard vector edges.
detail_level: Moderate: the disk's flatness, the polar infall funnels and the truncated outer edge all clearly readable; texture painterly throughout.
composition: Star left of centre, disk sweeping rightward toward the companion at the right edge, truncation visible about two-thirds of the way across. Dark open cloud space along the top edge for callouts.
consistency_notes: No planets yet - this is the disk stage. The truncation on the companion's side must be visible as an abrupt edge, conveyed by shape alone with no drawn boundary line.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no orbit lines, no grid, no diagram chrome, no planets, no moons, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
